Importantly, it is the DDM’s error forecast for one Hydraulic Residence Time (HRT) in the future. 5.2.3 Get Data The HRSD NTP leverages its online digital twin (DT) to forecast the mechanistic model error based on historical data. This DT is a digital replica of the plant’s biological process, constructed using the Sumo software by Dynamita (Sigale, France). It receives real-time data from the facility's control system via the Open Platform Communications (OPC) protocol. This data includes a variety of parameters such as the influent flow rate, recycle flow rates, waste flow rate, methanol flow rates to the second stage anoxic zones, DO concentrations for all aerobic zones, and the raw influent temperature. The influent TKN concentration from the laboratory is also ingested by the DT. Every minute, the DT generates a new modelled NHx value, which is then compared to the corresponding measured value from the NHx analyzer. The difference between these two values constitutes the mechanistic model error. While the DT can produce a new modelled NHx every minute, the NHx analysis requires 20 minutes. Consequently, the time step interval chosen for the proof-of-concept modelling that is described in the following two sections was a 20-minute interval to align with the analyzer measurement frequency. 5.2.4 Prepare Data While technically a multivariate model, the DDM forecasting err relies solely on historical mech err data. Specifically, the model incorporates the current err value, its recent change mech mech between t-1 and t, and its rolling 24-hour statistical information (median, maximum, minimum). These features were selected based on their importance for overall model performance and, crucially, for accurately forecasting err peaks and valleys. Precisely forecasting these mech extremes is essential for calculating DO s that manage diurnal TKN load fluctuations and SP minimize controller errors. Note that given the low number of features, it was quite easy to surpass the recommended sample-to-feature ratio of 10-to-1. October 2023 err data were leveraged to establish the proof-of-concept. After a preliminary mech visual inspection to identify anomalies, the data underwent a smoothing process using a Savitzky-Golay filter, known for its wide application for instrument signal smoothing.
